name: Gaius
title: The Hospitable Believer
summary: Gaius was a faithful Christian praised by the apostle John for his hospitality and commitment to the truth. He welcomed and supported traveling preachers and missionaries, becoming an example of Christian love and service in the early church. The name Gaius is mentioned several times in the New Testament and may refer to different individuals.

keyEvents.title: John's Greeting to Gaius
keyEvents.description: The apostle John writes his third letter to his dear friend Gaius, expressing his love and care for him.

keyEvents.title: Gaius's Walk in the Truth
keyEvents.description: John rejoices at the reports that Gaius walks in the truth, declaring that nothing gives him greater joy than hearing that his children live in the truth.

keyEvents.title: Gaius's Hospitality to Traveling Brothers
keyEvents.description: Gaius is praised for his faithful service to the believers, especially foreign brothers who traveled around preaching the gospel. He welcomed them and sent them on their way in a worthy manner.

keyEvents.title: The Contrast with Diotrephes
keyEvents.description: In contrast to Gaius' hospitality, Diotrephes refused to welcome the brothers and expelled from the church those who wanted to help. John warns Gaius not to imitate what is evil.

keyEvents.title: Gaius of Corinth as Paul's Host
keyEvents.description: Paul mentions a Gaius in Corinth who was his host and that of the whole church, and who was one of the few Paul personally baptized.

keyEvents.title: Gaius of Derbe as Travel Companion
keyEvents.description: A Gaius from Derbe is mentioned as one of Paul's travel companions during his third missionary journey and was among those involved in the riots in Ephesus.
